text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The high court has subpoenaed police inspector general Patrick Chikapa for allegedly asking his deputy to ignore a summons to answer contempt of court charges on the rearrest of four Nigerians freed on bail.
- The U.N. High Commission for Refugees in Malawi contradicted the Malawi government and said the country could not refuse asylum to refugees from neighbouring countries.
- Sugar prices soared unofficially by nearly 100 percent.
- Car dealer Apex Car Sales has impounded eight of the nine minibuses sold to supporters of the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) for defaulting a weekly payment of 8,000 kwacha for each vehicle.

- The opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) has accepted an offer by a group of bishops to mediate the country's political impasse between the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) and two opposition parties.
- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) vice president Gwanda Chakuamba said he hoped the meeting with the clergy would help resolve the political impasse.
